claims.text: Interfacial strain governs the magnetocaloric response of nanoscale as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi films or nanoribbons during low-field cooling cycles.
Limited heat dissipation governs hysteresis and magnetocaloric response in these low-dimensional alloys.
Interfacial strain and limited heat dissipation hinder a uniform magneto-structural phase transformation.
A uniform magneto-structural phase transformation occurs in relevant bulk forms of the alloy.
The as-deposited films or nanoribbons exhibit intrinsic microstructural strain.
The as-deposited films or nanoribbons exhibit thermal interfacial resistance.
A Cu or graphene capping layer can enhance heat transfer from the active alloy.
Applying the capping layer can partially relieve interfacial stresses.
Local interfacial strain fields control magnetic-domain mobility.
Grain-boundary configurations control magnetic-domain mobility.
Local strain fields and grain boundaries act as barriers to a uniform phase transformation.
Improved heat flow from the capped active material reduces thermal gradients.
Reduced thermal gradients decrease associated local stresses.
Reduced thermal gradients and local stresses facilitate a more homogeneous, equilibrium magneto-structural transformation.
A more homogeneous magneto-structural transformation reduces hysteresis.
A more homogeneous magneto-structural transformation sharpens the magnetocaloric response.
Capped films or nanoribbons will have lower hysteresis width than untreated as-deposited controls.
Capped films or nanoribbons will exhibit a more pronounced and sharper magnetocaloric response than untreated controls.
The improved magnetocaloric response of capped samples will persist at faster cycling rates.
Intrinsic heat-transfer rates limit the applicable cycling frequency.
